Quick sizing notes (high level) — attaching a short dev_sizing_notes.pdf with the math. TL;DR recommendations below are conservative and assume mixed model usage and a moderate KV hit ratio.

Assumptions we used:
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + response): 680 tokens.
- Avg tokens/sec per active session (estimate, including thinking time): 6–8 tokens/sec.
- Steady-state traffic: 60k calls/day => ~0.7 RPS average, but traffic is spiky.
- Burst profile: 1.2k RPS sustained for 4–6 minutes (p95).

Conservative baseline (production, predictable spend):
- 6 x A100 80GB (reserved) configured as serving pool for 13B fast-path and batched 70B quantized variants.
- Expected steady concurrency headroom: ~70–120 concurrent chats (depends on batching).
- Cost: mid-range reserved monthly estimate (see PDF).

Resilient + burst plan (handles micro-bursts):
- Baseline: 4 x A100 80GB reserved.
- Burst pool: 4 x H100 80GB (on-demand or Dedicated burst nodes) that spin up via reserved capacity + short-term burst allowance. H100s for lower tail latency during bursts and better multiquery throughput.
- Autoscale + prefix KV cache: recommend putting session prefixes into the KV cache (expect 20–35% token savings on repeated context).
- Use 4-bit quant for 70B to reduce memory footprint; keep 13B at 8-bit or fp16 for quality.

Operational recommendations:
- Enable continuous batching with a short max batch latency (40–75ms) to preserve p95 latency while getting token-economy benefits.
- Stream responses where applicable so perceived latency is lower for users.
- Canary: start with 2 reserved A100s + 1 burst H100, run synthetic burst test and shadow traffic before expanding.

Attachments: dev_sizing_notes.pdf, greenwave_arch_diagram.png

Happy to walk through the math — Dev

Subject: Proposed first-pass footprint and next steps (GW-2028-71)

Hi Maria / Evan — thanks for the quick turnaround on the workbook. Based on your fills and Dev's math, here's a conservative first-pass we can use for procurement and technical validation: 

Baseline (predictable spend):
- Reserved: 6 x A100 80GB serving pool (13B + quantized 70B). Good for steady concurrency and cost predictability.
- Expected steady concurrency coverage: ~80 concurrent chats with standard batching (latency p95 ~350–450ms depending on prompt mix).

Burst-handling configuration (preserves UX during launches):
- Keep 4 x H100 80GB burst nodes available (burst pool). Configure smart routing: requests route to baseline pool by default; when queue depth or latency exceeds thresholds, route to burst pool. Use autoscale + short reservation or on-demand burst credits for the H100s.

Cost/caveats:
- Quantizing 70B to 4-bit materially reduces memory footprint but may introduce small quality regressions — recommend A/B evals on 200 prompt set.
- KV cache for session prefixes will likely reduce token throughput by ~20–30% for their multi-turn flows — important for lowering steady-state cost.

Next steps I propose:
1) Schedule a 30-minute technical call to validate burst shape and canary plan (Thu 2:30pm PT works for us).
2) Run a 10-minute synthetic burst test in a sandbox (we can provision burst H100s for this).
3) Run a short A/B on quantized vs fp16 70B replicas using their prompt set.

Marissa will follow up with a pricing sketch (reserved vs burst addons) and a simple rollout checklist. Attaching the Q&A they filled and our sizing notes for your procurement team.

Best,
Soojin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: gw_rightsize_qna.xlsx, dev_sizing_notes.pdf
